newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Stals says budget paves way for rate cut.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Stals says budget paves way for rate cut.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Friday that a tight 1997/98 budget paved the way for a possible cut in interest rates later this year.
"Just about everything in this budget moved in the right direction to make monetary policy easier," he told parliament's finance committee.

Stals said the reduction in the budget deficit as a percentage of GDP to four percent from over five percent and the actual fall in the gross borrowing requirement to 36.85 billion rand from 41.02 billion would help considerably in cutting government demands on the market.

"This is certainly going to reduce the total demand for funds in the market. There will be more funds available for private sector economic development, therefore there will be less demand for bank credit and in the whole process less pressure on interest rates."
But Stals said he remained concerned that government was still dissaving and the deficit before borrowing needed to be reduced to around two percent of GDP to equal capital expenditure.
